gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-ethiopi: Heavy, bent-straw letters with curls that nearly close. Noto Sans Ethiopic sits beside them with hanging c terminals and a tall, sturdy lowercase, so the open body feels like a deep breath after the dense heading.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-georgia: Plakkaat draws every letter in one unbroken, heavy line, with terminals curling nearly back to the stem. Noto Sans Georgian answers with lighter, open curves.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-glagoli: Noto Sans Glagolitic reads friendly and open, its round letters staying legible even when the text gets small. Over a long stretch it keeps a tall, sturdy lowercase, while Plakkaat stays heavy above.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic opens wide, its round forms curving like parentheses. Plakkaat's heavy, uninterrupted lines stay closed up above, so the two feel like a shout followed by an easy conversation.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Noto Sans Grantha reads smoothly, with tall little bowls that never clog. Make Plakkaat small or the plain sans large, and the heavy, closed heading loses the weight that sets the two apart.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-gujarat: Bent-straw heft up top, with curls that nearly seal shut against the stem. Noto Sans Gujarati keeps its curved strokes open below, so a long passage would feel unhurried and light after the heavy heading.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-gunjala: Plakkaat's terminals sweep round until they almost touch the stem. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi, a plain sans with tall strokes and cut-back ends, would read in a loose, contemporary way over a longer stretch.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-gurmukh: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads clean, its outward-pointing terminals like tongs and ascenders barely clearing the x-height. Across a longer passage it feels compact and steady, a quiet foil to Plakkaat's heavy, bent-straw heading.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Plakkaat is heavy and unbroken, its curls closing almost to the stem. Noto Sans Hanunoo, a plain sans filling most of the line height with open terminals, is the one to read, while Plakkaat is the one to notice.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Plakkaat is bold and tightly curled, with low contrast and closed letters. Noto Sans Hebrew, a plain sans with a dominant midsection and wide gaps near the stems, handles the reading while Plakkaat grabs the eye.
